title: Tapas de última hora en Lavapiés

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: ¡Hola, Javi! Bueno, ¿qué tal el curro hoy? Te veo con una cara de cansado impresionante.
dialogue.english: Hi, Javi! Well, how was work today? You look completely exhausted.

slang.actualMeaning: work / job (everyday colloquial word in Spain)
slang.example: Salgo del curro a las seis y nos vemos en el centro.

dialogue.speaker: Javi
dialogue.spanish: Uf, ni me hables, tía. Pues estuve súper liado con un informe toda la tarde, pero ya me muero de hambre.
dialogue.english: Phew, don't even get me started, girl. Well I was super tied up with a report all afternoon, but now I'm starving.

slang.example: Perdona que no te llamara, anduve súper liado toda la mañana.

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Venga, entremos a esta taberna de la esquina que ponen unas patatas bravas que flipas por cinco euros.
dialogue.english: Come on, let's go into this corner tavern—they serve mind-blowing patatas bravas for five euros.

slang.example: En ese bar hacen una tortilla de patatas que flipas.

dialogue.speaker: Javi
dialogue.spanish: ¡Ostras, qué buena pinta! O sea, ¿también tienen croquetas caseras de jamón?
dialogue.english: Whoa, that sounds great! I mean, do they also have homemade ham croquettes?

dialogue.speaker: Lucía
dialogue.spanish: Sí, la ración de seis croquetas sale a ocho euros y viene con pan recién tostado.
dialogue.english: Yes, a plate of six croquettes is eight euros and comes with freshly toasted bread.

dialogue.speaker: Javi
dialogue.spanish: ¡De lujo! Pide tú dos cañas bien frías en la barra mientras busco una mesa libre al fondo.
dialogue.english: Awesome! You order two ice-cold draft beers at the bar while I look for an empty table in the back.

questions.question: Why does Javi look so tired when he meets Lucía?
options: He was swamped working on a report all afternoon
He walked all the way across Madrid in the rain
He stayed up late watching a soccer match
He just came back from the gym
questions.explanation: Javi explains: 'estuve súper liado con un informe toda la tarde' (he was swamped with a report all afternoon).

questions.question: What two dishes do they plan to order at the tavern, and what do they cost?
options: Patatas bravas for 5 euros and six ham croquettes for 8 euros
Spanish tortilla for 10 euros and calamari for 12 euros
Olives for 3 euros and paella for 18 euros
questions.explanation: Lucía mentions patatas bravas for 5 euros and a plate of six ham croquettes for 8 euros.

questions.question: What does Javi ask Lucía to order at the bar while he looks for a table?
options: Two cold draft beers ('dos cañas bien frías')
questions.explanation: Javi says: 'Pide tú dos cañas bien frías en la barra mientras busco una mesa libre al fondo.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: In Spain, what do 'el curro', 'estar súper liado', and 'que flipas' mean?
options: 'El curro' = work/job; 'súper liado' = swamped/busy; 'que flipas' = mind-blowing/amazing
'El curro' = the bus; 'súper liado' = lost; 'que flipas' = overpriced
'El curro' = the boss; 'súper liado' = hungry; 'que flipas' = very spicy
'El curro' = the gym; 'súper liado' = sleepy; 'que flipas' = frozen
questions.explanation: In Spain, 'el curro' means work, 'estar liado' means to be busy/swamped, and 'que flipas' means amazing/mind-blowing!
